description: string wrapped in matching quotes

On the feedback form, the short summary box must be a non-empty string of at most 12 words. Words are separated by single spaces, with no leading or trailing whitespace and no consecutive spaces. Each word is made of ordinary ASCII letters and may end with a single comma or period, but that punctuation must not be followed by another punctuation mark or attached to the middle of a word.
failed_match: One two three four five six seven eight nine ten eleven twelve
a b c d e f g h i j k l

description: Validate a sentence: it must start with an uppercase letter (A-Z), followed by any number of characters that are not periods, and must end with exactly one period. The period is the only allowed punctuation at the end, and no other periods may appear in the sentence.
failed_match: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

description: A string is valid if it contains the whole word 'error' as a standalone word: 'error' must be preceded either by the start of the string or by a character that is not a letter, digit, or underscore, and followed either by the end of the string or by a character that is not a letter, digit, or underscore. The match may occur anywhere in the string; the whole string does not need to equal the word.

Our bio field on the profile page is a short tagline that must not exceed six words. Words are separated by single spaces. Every word consists only of Latin letters, and there may be no leading or trailing space. The field may also be left empty.

A sentence must start with a capital letter and end with a period. Any characters except a period are allowed in between, but there must be at least one character between the capital letter and the period.

Our pricing import tool reads a quantity field from supplier spreadsheets; it accepts a plain decimal number that may be negative and may have a fractional part, so an optional plus or minus sign followed by digits, optionally followed by a period and more digits, is required.

Validate a decimal number written in normalized scientific notation. Rules:
1. An optional leading minus sign is allowed; a leading plus sign is not.
2. The significand is either a single non-zero digit, or a non-zero digit followed by a decimal point and one or more digits.
3. A lowercase or uppercase "e" separates the significand from the exponent.
4. The exponent is an optional minus or plus sign followed by one or more digits, with no leading zeros unless the exponent is exactly zero.
5. The significand must not have leading zeros (the digit before the decimal point is 1-9), and no whitespace is allowed anywhere.

A percentage field must be a value from 0 to 100 inclusive, with an optional fractional part of at most two digits; when a fractional part is given it must be preceded by a decimal point, and the digits before that point must be either 0 or a whole number from 1 to 100 without leading zeros. A literal percent sign may optionally follow the number, with no space before it.

Scientific notation format: an optional sign, followed by a non-zero digit, then zero or more digits, an optional decimal point with at least one digit after it if present, then the letter 'e' (case-insensitive), an optional sign, and one or more digits. The entire string must conform to this format. No leading zeros are allowed in the coefficient's integer part unless it is zero, but here the integer part must start with a non-zero digit.
Every line in the input must be a non-empty sequence of digits (0-9). The input must have at least one line. Lines are separated by newline characters. No other characters are allowed.

We need to detect pasted notes that contain a paragraph break, meaning the text has at least one blank line somewhere in it (two consecutive line breaks, or a line break at the very beginning or end of the text).

The input must be a non-empty text where every line is an integer. Each line contains one or more digits, optionally starting with a minus sign, and nothing else. The text may end with a final newline.
text of at most three lines, lines separated by newlines

Conventional Commit subject: type required, one of feat/fix/docs/style/refactor/perf/test/build/ci/chore/revert (lowercase). Scope optional, lowercase hyphenated identifier. Breaking change optional: ! before colon. Then colon and space. Description must be non-empty, not start with uppercase, no trailing period.
error: Invalid regular expression: /^(?:feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|build|ci|chore|revert)(?:-[a-z]+)?!(?:?:|::| )[A-Z][A-Z0-9_\-]*[A-Z0-9_\-]*$/: Nothing to repeat

description: A git branch name should start with one of the prefixes feature/, bugfix/, or hotfix/, followed by a lowercase kebab-case description that consists of one or more words separated by single hyphens. Each word contains only lowercase letters and digits.

Our community signup needs a display name that works as a handle. It may contain letters, numbers, periods, dashes and underscores, but the first and last character must be a letter or a number, and the whole thing should be 4 to 16 characters long.
Validate an email address. The local part may contain letters (any case), digits, dots, underscores, percent signs, plus signs, and hyphens. The domain must be exactly example.com, case-insensitive.

We need to accept the email address entered in the newsletter subscription form. A valid address has exactly one @, the local part consists of letters, digits, and the following special characters: dot, underscore, percent, plus, hyphen. The domain part consists of one or more dot-separated labels, where each label starts and ends with a letter or digit and may contain hyphens in between, and the final label (top-level domain) is at least two letters. No other restrictions apply; only the format is checked.

Our newsletter signup needs a quick sanity check on the email address field so we can tell obviously bogus entries from real ones before sending a confirmation message. An address should look like a typical personal or business email: a non-empty local part made of ordinary characters, a single @, and a domain with at least one dot whose final part is at least two letters.

Match a US date in the format MM/DD/YYYY or MM-DD-YYYY. The month, day, and year must be separated by either slashes or dashes, but not a mix. The month is one or two digits, from 1 to 12. The day is one or two digits, from 1 to 31. The year is exactly four digits.
Month abbreviation: exactly one of the twelve three-letter English month abbreviations, case-insensitive: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun, Jul, Aug, Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec.
Match a European date in day/month/year format. The day and month are written with one or two digits, the year with exactly four digits, and the three parts are separated by forward slashes.

US-format date mm/dd/yyyy. Rules: the month is two digits from 01 to 12; the day is two digits from 01 to 31; the year is exactly four digits. Slashes separate the three parts. No other characters are allowed, and the string must be exactly the date.

Match a UK postcode. It consists of an outward code of one or two letters, followed by one or two digits, optionally followed by a letter, then a space, and an inward code of one digit followed by two letters. The letters are case-insensitive and the space is required.
uk postcode strict
Match a Portuguese VAT number: nine digits, optionally prefixed by PT, with optional spaces or dots between the digits and after the prefix.
french SIRET (14 digits) or SIREN (9 digits), no spaces

Our Canadian checkout needs to accept the postal code customers enter on the shipping form; it should be the standard six-character Canadian postal code, with an optional single space between the two halves.
french number 10 digits starting with 0
we only take french mobile numbers, ten digits starting with 06 or 07, spaces allowed between pairs

UK mobile number field.
- National format: 11 digits starting with 07.
- International format: optional +44 or 0044 prefix followed by the 10-digit national number without the leading 0 (i.e. starting with 7).
- A single space may optionally separate the prefix from the rest, and in the national format spaces may optionally separate digits in groups of any size.
- No other characters are allowed.
Match an E.164 international phone number. It starts with a plus sign, followed by a non-zero digit, then up to 14 more digits.
We need to validate the amount field for our Japanese store; all prices are in yen and we never deal with sen, so only whole numbers are accepted.

Our storefront needs a price field where customers type amounts in euros. The price must be a plain number with exactly two decimal digits after the dot, and at least one digit before it; no thousands separators, currency symbols, or signs are allowed.

A euro price in French formatting, where thousands are separated by spaces in groups of three, the decimal part uses a comma and always has two digits, and the amount ends with a space and the euro symbol.

Validate a price in euros in French format with these rules: it must be a positive amount strictly greater than zero, using a comma as decimal separator, exactly two decimal digits if a decimal part is present, groups of three digits separated by a space starting from the right, and a trailing euro sign preceded by a space. The integer part may not have leading zeros unless it is exactly zero, but if it is zero then the decimal part must be present and not all zeros. Also, the space used as thousands separator must be a regular space, not a non-breaking space.

We need to validate the 'amount' field in our accounting system. Valid amounts are non-negative numbers with exactly two decimal places (dot as decimal separator, no thousands separators). Negative amounts are represented in accounting format: the absolute value enclosed in parentheses, e.g., (123.45) for -123.45. No plus sign allowed. The field must be a single line.
price optionally prefixed with a dollar sign, digits with thousands separated by commas and exactly two decimals

We need to validate monetary amounts entered in US dollars in our e-commerce checkout. The amount should be a positive number, optionally with a dollar sign, and may include commas as thousand separators. If cents are provided, they must be exactly two digits. No spaces allowed.
private ipv4 addresses, 192.168.x.x only

We store the IPv6 address our customers type in when they register a device. It has to be the full eight-group form, each group being exactly four hexadecimal digits, groups separated by colons; the :: shorthand and any abbreviated groups are not accepted.

We need to check the hostname field in our server setup form. A hostname is a dot-separated list of labels, each of which starts and ends with a letter or digit and may contain letters, digits, and hyphens in between. No label may be empty, longer than 63 characters, or begin with a hyphen. The whole hostname must be 253 characters or fewer and must not end with a dot.
Match a TCP or UDP port number. It must be a whole number from 1 to 65535, written in decimal without a leading plus sign, leading zeros, or any other characters.
An IPv4 CIDR block: a dotted-quad IPv4 address (four decimal octets 0-255, no leading zeros) followed by a slash and a prefix length from 0 to 32 written without leading zeros.

Match an IPv4 CIDR block: a dotted-decimal IPv4 address with each octet from 0 to 255 and no leading zeros, followed by a slash and a prefix length from 0 to 32 written without leading zeros except for the single digit 0.

Validate an IPv4 address in dotted-decimal notation. The address must consist of exactly four octets separated by dots. Each octet must be a decimal number from 0 to 255, with no leading zeros unless the octet is exactly "0". No other characters are allowed.

Our deployment script needs to identify hidden configuration files so it can skip them. A hidden file name starts with a dot, followed by at least one character that is not a slash, and ends with .conf. The entire string must be just the file name, with no directory separators.

Our backup tool needs to identify hidden files on Unix-like systems. A hidden file name must start with a dot, followed by at least one character that is not a dot or a slash. The name may contain additional dots, letters, digits, underscores, or hyphens, but it must not be just a dot or two dots (i.e., . and .. are not considered valid hidden file names).

jest or vitest test files - basename must be nonempty with no leading dot or dash, dot separators only, extension .js .jsx .ts or .tsx and the segment right before it exactly spec or test; reject .spec.ts.bak, double dots, and names like .spec.ts
error: not a single ES2018 regex literal

description:
Password policy specification:
1. Length must be between 8 and 64 characters inclusive.
2. Allowed characters are ASCII letters, digits, and the symbols ! @ # $ % ^ & * ( ) - _ = + [ ] { } ; : , . ? / \ | ~ ` ' " < >.
3. The password must not contain the substring "password" in any letter casing (for example, "Password", "PASSWORD", "PassWord" are all forbidden).
4. The password must not contain whitespace of any kind.
error: not a single ES2018 regex literal

description: For the new recovery codes we want users to type a phrase instead of a password: it has to be made of four or more words with a single space between them. Only letters count as word characters.

A passphrase must consist of at least four words. Each word is composed of letters (a-z, A-Z) and must be separated from the next by a single space. The entire passphrase must match this pattern, with no leading or trailing spaces.

A person's name in any script may contain letters, spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, and periods. It must start with a letter and may not end with a space or hyphen. At least one letter is required, but the whole name may be a single letter.
number using any Unicode decimal digits

Our mapping widget needs to accept a latitude typed into the location field. The value is in decimal degrees and may be negative for the southern hemisphere; a positive value may optionally start with a plus sign. At most six digits after the decimal point are kept. Values outside the range from 90 degrees south to 90 degrees north must be rejected, and a bare sign or a trailing decimal point is not a valid entry.
the product page needs a resolution field that reads like 1920x1080, two whole numbers separated by a lower-case x, no spaces and no thousands separators

We need to validate weight entries in a logistics system. The weight must be a non-negative number (integer or decimal with up to two decimal places) followed by a space and either 'kg' or 'g'. The numeric value must be greater than 0. Leading zeros are allowed only if the number is less than 1 (e.g., 0.5 kg) but zero itself is invalid. Also, decimal values less than 1 must be written with a leading zero (e.g., .5 kg is not allowed). The unit is case-sensitive: 'kg' and 'g' must be lowercase. No trailing spaces or extra characters.

Our recipe site's temperature field should accept a temperature followed by its unit: the number may be negative, decimals are allowed, and the unit is either the degree symbol with C or F, or just C or F. A space before the unit is optional. Only Celsius and Fahrenheit are valid.
image size like 3840x2160 or 1024x768, width and height positive integers with no leading zeros
Match a latitude given as decimal degrees. The value must be between -90 and 90 inclusive, an optional plus or minus sign may come first, and up to six digits after the decimal point are allowed.
match a file size: number with optional one decimal, space, then B, KB, MB, GB, or TB in any case, no leading zeros except zero itself
weight like 12kg or 500g
Match a valid JavaScript identifier, allowing the dollar sign and underscore in addition to letters and digits; the first character must not be a digit, and the string must be entirely ASCII.

Our backend service uses environment variables for configuration, and we need to validate the names of these variables in our deployment pipeline. The names must be snake_case (all lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, starting with a letter) or SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (all uppercase letters, digits, and underscores, starting with an uppercase letter). Additionally, the name must not contain two consecutive underscores, and it must not start or end with an underscore. Also, the name must not be a single underscore alone. For example, 'my_var' and 'MY_VAR' are valid, but '_my_var', 'my__var', 'MyVar', and 'my_var_' are invalid.
kebab case with no double hyphen, no leading or trailing hyphen, lowercase letters and digits only

Identifier must be either snake_case or SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE:
- Only ASCII letters, digits and underscores are allowed.
- It must not start with a digit and must not consist solely of digits.
- It must not start or end with an underscore, and it must not contain two or more consecutive underscores.
- Either all letters are lowercase with at least one underscore present, or all letters are uppercase with at least one underscore present.
Validate an order reference consisting of exactly 6 decimal digits. The reference must not end in the digit 0. Only the format is checked.

Validate filenames that must consist of one or more characters from the set [a-zA-Z0-9_], with an optional extension starting with a dot followed by one or more letters. The extension must not be 'exe' or 'dll' (case-insensitive).
A word consisting of lowercase letters that is not one of: if, else, for, while, return.

In the loyalty program, a member's point balance is stored as a whole number written without any separators. Members who have been flagged as at-risk must not have balances that end in the digit seven, since that value is reserved for a promotional code collision. A valid balance is a non-negative integer of up to nine digits that does not end in seven.
log file names, must not end in .tmp or .log (any case), letters digits underscore dash dot allowed, no leading dot

We're building a lightweight settings field where users paste a list of numeric IDs. The field must accept only a JSON array containing one or more numbers, where each number is either a whole number or a decimal, and negative values are allowed. No extra whitespace or other content is permitted.

We store tiny XML-like snippets and need to confirm that a snippet we received opens and closes a single tag with no content between them, and that the closing tag uses exactly the same tag name as the opening one. Tag names are one or more word characters, letters, digits or underscore. The whole string must be just the opening tag, then the closing tag, with nothing else and no whitespace.

1. The string is a list of one or more integers separated by commas with no spaces.
2. Each integer is an optional minus sign followed by one or more digits.
3. A leading zero is allowed only if the integer is exactly "0"; otherwise no leading zeros, and "-0" is not allowed.
4. The string must not start or end with a comma, and no empty elements.

We need to verify that an authentication token string has the correct compact serialization shape for a JWT: three parts separated by dots, where each part is a non-empty sequence of characters from the Base64URL alphabet (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, - and _). The string must contain no other characters, and there must be exactly three parts.

A well-formed XML-ish tag pair occupying the entire string: an opening tag, some text content, then a closing tag. An opening tag is an angle bracket, a tag name, optionally a space followed by an attribute list, then a closing angle bracket. The tag name must begin with a letter and may continue with letters, digits, hyphens, or underscores. The attribute list is one or more attributes separated by single spaces; each attribute is a name (same naming rule as tag names) followed by an equals sign and a double-quoted value containing any characters except a double quote. The closing tag is an angle bracket, a slash, the same tag name as the opening tag, and a closing angle bracket. The content between the tags may be any characters except an opening angle bracket.

A string consisting of an opening tag and a matching closing tag. A tag is written as a name enclosed in angle brackets, where the name starts with an ASCII letter or underscore and continues with ASCII letters, digits, underscores, hyphens, or periods. The opening and closing tags must share exactly the same name and use the same letter case. No attributes, whitespace, or content may appear between or around the tags.
Match a JWT: three Base64URL-encoded segments separated by dots. Each segment must contain at least one character and may consist only of letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores.

We want to pull out frames of a Java-style call stack from a captured error report. A frame line matches only when the line consists solely of whitespace followed by 'at' between word boundaries, then whitespace, then a fully qualified method name: one or more dot-separated identifiers starting with a dollar sign, letter, or underscore. The method name continues with a parenthesized suffix holding either the literal 'Native Method', the literal 'Unknown Source', or a file name ending in '.java' followed by a colon and one or more digits. Leading whitespace is allowed, but trailing characters after the closing parenthesis are not.

We need to scan application log lines for error codes that our support team uses to track incidents. An error code is a token that starts with the letters 'ERR' in uppercase, followed by a hyphen, and then exactly three digits. The code may appear anywhere in the line, but it must be a separate token, not part of a larger word like 'ERR-1234' or 'XERR-123'. However, punctuation like brackets or commas around it is fine. We only care about the format; no checksum or validity check is needed.

Our release pipeline needs to accept a user-supplied release number in the field where we store the semantic version of a build. A valid value is a major, minor, and patch number separated by periods, each one or more digits with no leading zeros unless the number is exactly zero. The value may optionally be followed by a hyphen and a prerelease tag made of dot-separated identifiers, where each identifier is either all digits (no leading zeros unless zero) or alphanumeric starting with a letter, and the whole prerelease part is required to be present if the hyphen is present. Build metadata is not accepted.

Match a git tag that starts with a lowercase v, followed by a major version number, a dot, a minor version number, and optionally a dot and a patch version number. The major, minor, and patch numbers are one or more digits and may have leading zeros.

Our release pipeline reads tag names from a webhook payload, and we only want to trigger deployments for tags that follow our versioning convention. A tag is valid when it starts with a lowercase v, followed by either two or three dot-separated numeric components where each component is one or more digits with no leading zero (a lone zero is fine), and nothing else — no extra suffixes, no whitespace, no uppercase V.
we tag our releases in git like v1.2 or v1.2.3, but the numbers must not have leading zeros (so v1.02 is not allowed) and the tag cannot be just v with no numbers

Our app uses a client-side router and we need to detect links that are meant to navigate within the site. These links always start with a single forward slash, followed by path segments separated by slashes; each segment can contain letters, digits, hyphens, underscores, and dots, but cannot be empty, and the whole path must not end with a slash. A query string starting with ? and/or a fragment starting with # may follow the path, containing any characters except spaces.

Our design system tokens accept CSS length values, but only the units we support in the web app: px, em, rem, %, vw, vh. The numeric part can be any non-negative number, including decimals, and may be preceded by a plus sign. No spaces are allowed between the number and the unit. The value must be the entire string.
Match a CSS hex color written with either three or six hexadecimal digits, preceded by a hash.

Validate a CSS length value. Rules: a non-negative number is allowed, either an integer or a decimal with a fractional part, where the integer part may be omitted as long as the fractional part exists; the number must be followed by one of the units px, em, rem, vh, vw, or % ; neither leading plus signs nor whitespace are allowed.

Our link checker needs to accept web addresses that begin with either the http or https scheme, followed by a host, an optional port, and an optional path. The scheme must be followed by ://; the host must be composed of dot-separated labels of alphanumeric characters and hyphens, with the last label at least two characters long, and it may not start with a hyphen. A port, if present, is written as a colon followed by one to five digits. The path, if present, starts with a slash and then contains any non-space characters. Whitespace is not allowed anywhere in the address.
domain ending in .co.uk
git commit hash either 7 or 40 lowercase hex chars

A ticket reference consists of an uppercase project key of 2 to 10 letters, a hyphen, and a positive integer issue number (no leading zeros, maximum 9999). The project key must contain only uppercase letters A-Z. Examples: 'ABC-123', 'PROJ-7'. The issue number must be at least 1 and at most 9999.
An internal product code must match exactly: two uppercase letters, a hyphen, then four digits, for example the shape AA-0000. Nothing else is accepted.

A SHA-256 hex digest is written as exactly 64 hexadecimal characters with no separators; uppercase letters are allowed as an alternative to lowercase. Match a string that is exactly one such digest, but reject strings that merely contain a digest within other text.

We need to validate a UUID (Universally Unique Identifier) that is in its standard 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal format and specifically version 4 (random). The version number is the first character of the third group and must be '4'. The variant is the first character of the fourth group and must be one of 8, 9, A, B, a, or b. All other characters are hexadecimal digits. No braces or other delimiters are allowed.

Product SKU format:
- Must start with two uppercase letters (category code).
- Followed by a hyphen.
- Then a 4-digit number (0000-9999).
- Then a hyphen.
- Then exactly 3 uppercase letters (variant code).
- No other characters allowed.
- Example: AB-1234-XYZ

A product SKU must follow the pattern: the first character is an uppercase letter from A to Z, followed by exactly three digits (0-9), then a hyphen, then two uppercase letters from A to Z (but not 'XX', which is reserved and forbidden), and finally a single digit (0-9). The entire string must be this exact format with no extra characters. The reserved sequence 'XX' is not allowed in the two-letter part.

The string must be a version 3 UUID in canonical form: five lowercase hexadecimal groups separated by hyphens, with lengths 8, 4, 4, 4, and 12, where the first character of the third group is 3 and the first character of the fourth group is one of 8, 9, a, or b.
Match a non-empty string consisting only of hexadecimal digits whose total length is an even number.
